heading: 經國大典 禮典 · 喪葬 상장 · Mourning and Burial … 禮典 喪葬 2

items.text: Leave the grave undisturbed: do not plow or graze livestock within the set limits.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Yejeon Sangjang 2
items.quote: 墳墓, 定限禁耕牧。 — Set limits prohibiting cultivation and pasturage at graves.

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: succession, adoption, marriage, mourning, hous
heading: 經國大典 禮典 · 婚嫁 혼가 · Marriage … 禮典 婚嫁 6

items.text: Do not give a child in marriage before the lawful age; if a parent is chronically ill or has reached fifty, a child of twelve or older may marry after reporting to the office.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 男年十五, 女年十四, 方許婚嫁...若兩家父母中一人有宿疾或年滿五十而子女年十二以上者, 告官婚嫁。 — A son at fifteen, a daughter at fourteen, then marriage is allowed; if a parent of either family has a chronic illness or is fifty, children twelve or older may marry after reporting to the office.

items.text: Before arranging a marriage for a child of the royal clan, report the child's age and the other family's head to the Office of Royal Clan.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 宗室, 則具其子女年歲及定婚家主職·姓名, 告宗簿寺。 — For the royal clan, prepare the child's age and the other family head's office and name, and report to the Office of Royal Clan.

items.text: Do not arrange a marriage for a child under ten in the royal clan; if the age difference is six years and the child is unwilling, do not allow the match.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 兩家子女年滿十歲, 方許議婚。 年六歲相差而非情願者, 勿許相婚。 — Both families' children must be ten to discuss marriage; if the age difference is six years and not willing, do not allow the marriage.

items.text: Do not conceal or falsify a child's age in a marriage arrangement; if discovered, the head of the family will be punished.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 加減隱諱後現者, 家長以爲婚妄冒律論。 — If later found to have concealed or altered, the head of family is punished under the law for false marriage.

items.text: Do not remarry until three years after your wife's death; but if your parents command it or you are over forty with no son, you may remarry after one year.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 士大夫妻亡者, 三年後改娶, 若因父母之命或年過四十無子者, 許期年後改娶。 — For a scholar-official whose wife has died, remarry after three years; if by parents' command or over forty without a son, allowed after one year.
items.conflict: 1 Cor 7:39 — a spouse is free to remarry after death; no required waiting period.

items.text: When you are a new bride, go to your parents-in-law with wine, food, and attendants, as the rites require.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: Marriage 6
items.quote: 新婦謁舅姑, 酒一盆, 肴饌五器, 從婢三人, 奴十人。 — The new bride greets the parents-in-law with one basin of wine, five dishes, three maids, and ten servants.

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: succession, adoption, marriage, mourning, hous
heading: 經國大典 禮典 · 五服 오복 · The Five Mourning Grades (table of mourning by kin) · 禮典 五服 1

items.text: Wear sackcloth for three years; if a soldier or commoner, you may wear it one hundred days, but you may choose the full three years.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 斬衰三年；軍士及庶人, 服百日, 母同；軍士願行三年者, 聽 — Wear sackcloth for three years; soldiers and commoners wear it one hundred days, same for mother; soldiers may choose three years.

items.text: Wear sackcloth for three years; if father is alive, reduce to one year of mourning and resign office for three years of heart mourning.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 齊衰三年；父在, 則十一月而練, 十三月而祥, 十五月而禫, 解官心喪三年 — Sackcloth three years; if father alive, at eleven months practice, thirteen months auspicious, fifteen months purification, resign office and heart-mourn three years.

items.text: Mourn them one year; if father is dead and you are the direct heir, wear sackcloth three years for grandfather.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 齊衰不杖期；父卒, 則嫡孫, 服斬衰三年 — Sackcloth without staff one year; if father dead, the direct grandson wears sackcloth three years.

items.text: Mourn them one year.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 兄弟 — 本宗: 期年 — Brother/sister: one year.

items.text: Treat them as natural parents in mourning: wear the same grades and periods for them and their kin.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 爲所後父母及內·外親, 竝如親子, 其報服亦同 — For adoptive parents and their kin, all as natural child; reciprocal mourning likewise.

items.text: Reduce mourning for birth parents to one year, resign office and heart-mourn three years, and reduce all natal kin mourning one degree.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 爲所生父母服期, 解官心喪三年, 爲本宗諸親, 竝降一等 — For birth parents wear one year, resign office and heart-mourn three years, for all natal kin reduce one degree.

items.text: Reduce mourning for natal kin by one degree; if divorced and returns, mourn as if unmarried.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 爲出嫁女, 降本服一等, 姑·姊·妹·女·孫女嫁反者, 同未嫁 — For a married-out daughter reduce one degree; if aunt, sister, daughter, granddaughter married and returns, treat as unmarried.

items.text: During the three years of mourning, do not attend banquets or marry wives or concubines.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 勿與宴樂·娶妻妾 — Do not join feasts or marry wife or concubine.

items.text: Wear sackcloth for three years for the household head.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 妾爲家長: 斬衰三年 — Concubine for household head: sackcloth three years.
items.conflict: A man shall have one wife (Gen 2:24; 1 Tim 3:2)

items.text: Mourn them one year.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Li Dian, Five Mourning Grades 1
items.quote: 伯·叔父母 — 本宗: 期年 — Uncle/aunt: one year.

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites: succession, adoption, marriage, mourning, hous
heading: 經國大典 禮典 · 奉祀 봉사 · Ancestral Rites and the Ritual Heir … 禮典 奉祀 2

items.text: Offer the ancestral rites to three, two, or one generation of forebears according to your official rank.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 文·武官六品以上, 祭三代, 七品以下, 祭二代, 庶人, 則只祭考妣。 — Civil and military officials of rank 6 and above sacrifice to three generations; rank 7 and below to two; commoners only to parents.
items.needs_role: any man holding office; if the main heir is lower rank, a branch son with higher rank takes over the number of generations

items.text: If an ancestor was a meritorious subject, keep his spirit tablet permanently and continue to offer rites for him in a separate room.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 始爲功臣者, 代雖盡, 不遷, 別立一室。 — For one who first became a meritorious subject, even when generations are exhausted, do not remove his tablet but set up a separate room.

items.text: If your great-grandfather's tablet is due to be removed, and you are an uncle or elder brother still in mourning for him, include him in your own sacrifices.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 曾祖代盡當出, 則就伯·叔位服未盡者, 祭之。 — When the great-grandfather's generation is exhausted and his tablet is to be removed, then sacrifice to him at the place of an uncle or elder brother whose mourning is not yet ended.
items.needs_role: uncle or elder brother still in mourning

items.text: If your father had more than one wife, enshrine all of them together with him in the ancestral rites.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 士大夫二妻以上, 並祔。 — If a scholar-official had two or more wives, enshrine them all together.

items.text: Take up the ancestral rites in the prescribed order: first the eldest legitimate son, then other legitimate sons, then sons of concubines; among concubine sons, the son of a commoner concubine before a low-born concubine if the former has no heir.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 若嫡長子無後, 則衆子, 衆子無後, 則妾子奉祀。 良妾子無後, 則賤妾子承重。 — If the eldest legitimate son has no heir, other sons; if other sons have no heir, sons of concubines; if a commoner concubine's son has no heir, a low-born concubine's son inherits.
items.needs_role: legitimate and concubine sons in order

items.text: If you are a concubine's son who has inherited the ritual responsibility, offer rites to your own mother in a private room, and let this duty end with you.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 凡妾子承重者, 祭其母於私室, 止其身。 — All concubine's sons who inherit the responsibility sacrifice to their mother in a private room, and it stops with him.
items.needs_role: a concubine's son who inherits the ritual responsibility

items.text: Attach collateral relatives who died without heirs to your ancestral rites by offering to them together with the main sacrifices.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 旁親之無後者, 祔祭。 — For collateral relatives without heirs, attach them in sacrifice.

items.text: If your master without children assigned you by written document to perform his rites, carry them out faithfully.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Book of Rites, Ancestral Rites 2
items.quote: 士大夫無子女欲以奴婢·墓直主祭者, 從財主之意, 署文記, 使奉其祀。 — If a scholar-official without children wishes slaves or tomb keepers to preside over rites, follow the owner's will, write a document, and have them perform his rites.
